name: amazon_product_camoufox
description: UPDATE 2026-09-05 (version 3): rating's regex is now the locale-free `(\d[.,]\d)` amazon_search uses, so '4,2 von 5 Sternen' parses; the 'out of' / English-only failures described below are history. Amazon product detail page. Pulls title, price, rating, availability, brand, feature bullets. Works across .com / .co.uk / .de / .fr / .co.jp. ENGINE: Camoufox, fingerprint_profile=windows_on_host — a Windows claim over this host's real AMD GPU vendor. Windows rather than the honest Linux because measurement put an honest Linux claim at 15 and 23 retries against 1 and 8 for Windows (see src/browser/fingerprint_profile.py). MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): 6/6 runs returned data on both engines across de/uk/us. Of the NINE declared fields, rating is the only one that ever came back null — on the de run here that was served German, and on both de runs of the Chromium twin — so every declared field filled on 5/6 runs here and 4/6 on the twin. That null is engine-neutral: rating's post-process regex matches only the English 'out of' phrasing, so it fails on any German-language page. The de run that announced locale en-DE got Amazon's English page and recorded price 3299.0 for price_raw '€32.99', because the price parser takes its decimal convention from the preset's declared country, not from the page. PREFER amazon_product_chromium, which derives its locale from the proxy country, announced de-DE on both de runs and parsed 32.99. The margin is the single de run that drew en-DE — the other drew bar-DE and Amazon still served German — so n=2 cannot say how often the damaging draw recurs; uk and us were indistinguishable across engines. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): 6/6 runs returned data with all NINE declared fields present on every run, unchanged (the harness's entries=7 is the length of the LONGEST list in the payload, len(bullets), not a field count). What changed is the de pair: both de runs now announce de-DE (08-27 drew en-DE and bar-DE), Amazon served German both times, and price parsed 32.99 against price_raw '32,99€' on both -- the 3299.0 hundred-fold error is gone, and across BOTH engines 0 of 12 amazon_product runs disagree with their own price_raw (08-27: 1 of 12). The locale pin has a cost, stated as measured: with the English page no longer drawn, rating is now null on BOTH de runs here (2/6, was 1/6), because rating's regex matches only the English 'out of' phrasing. That is the same 2/6 the Chromium twin has always had -- on de the two variants are now indistinguishable, so the PREFER note above no longer separates them on price. uk/us unchanged (rating 4.4 / 4.3, price 31.99 / 29.99, all nine fields). SCHEMA (final review): `rating` now declares its item type as [number, null], not number. It measured null on 3 of 12 runs in the 08-27 record and 4 of 12 in the 08-28 one, across both engines -- the English-only 'out of' regex meeting a German page -- and this preset sets self_heal: true, which hands `output_schema` to the LLM as the target contract (parser_pipeline.run -> generate_selectors). A schema claiming a field can never be null therefore steers a heal against the only behaviour this field has ever been measured to have. Same reason amazon_search's prices/ratings are nullable; this documents the null, it does not fix the regex.
